subject: Discovery recap: streaming latency & concurrency constraints for FinAgile
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@finagile.com>, Priya Raman <priya.r@finagile.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: streaming latency & concurrency constraints for FinAgile

Hi Oliver / Priya — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned. I captured the key pain points your team called out, success criteria, and a suggested technical deep dive scope for next week.

Summary of pain points (what we heard)
- Interactive streaming UX is choppy for live assistants — long initial first-byte delays and intermittent stalls when multiple users are active.
- P95 end-to-end response for streaming start is currently ~520ms and degrades during peaks. Your goal is a p95 < 200ms for first token in the majority of “agent assist” flows.
- Concurrency bursts: product expects ~400 concurrent live streams at peak, with occasional spikes to 1,000.
- Cost sensitivity: currently running larger models on dedicated hosts; team needs levers to lower unit cost without hurting quality (quantization, caching, smaller variants).

Current stack & traces you shared
- On-prem Kubernetes cluster (EKS-like) with GPU pool backed by A100s (you noted some nodes are older V100-equivalents).
- Inference stack: custom gRPC frontend -> in-house batching layer -> model server (PyTorch/XLA-based) -> Redis for session state.
- You uploaded a short perf snapshot (we have the CSV in the shared Drive).

Success criteria (what would make a win)
- p95 first-byte for streaming < 200ms under steady load.
- System supports 400 sustained concurrent streams with safe headroom for 1,000 spikes.
- No perceptible stall during token streaming (max stall < 150ms).
- Cost target: reduce per-request unit cost by 20–30% vs current baseline.

Proposed next steps
1) Technical deep-dive (60–90m) with your infra + product engineers and our runtime lead (Rishi) to review traces, batching patterns, and concurrency model.
2) Share a short set of sample traces and a single request/response recording (you mentioned the agent assist flow recorder) — we’ll ingest and reproduce in our test harness.
3) Draft a 3-week PoC scope focused on: (a) first-byte latency optimizations, (b) concurrency behavior under streaming, and (c) cost-saving knobs (quantization + caching).

Proposed timeline
- Deep-dive: week of Jan 19 (please confirm best slots)
- PoC kickoff: target Jan 26

Action items from today
- Oliver/Priya: upload the perf CSV + a short session trace (we have received finagile_perf_summary_q4.csv — thanks).
- Camila/Rishi: prep deep-dive agenda and a lightweight PoC doc (I attached proposed-poc-config.md).

If that aligns, I’ll schedule the deep-dive and include a pre-read. Appreciate quick confirmation on available slots for Jan 19–21.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: streaming latency & concurrency constraints for FinAgile

Camila — this is very helpful, thanks for the thorough read. Quick clarifications and a couple of notes from our infra team after running the perf snapshot overnight.

Clarifications
- That ~520ms p95 was measured from our frontend (post-auth) to first token emitted to the client. We see a wide variance across model variants (smaller variant ~230ms, large gen model ~820ms).
- The concurrency numbers: our product team expects 400 concurrent active sessions for the next quarter; finance wanted to budget for 1,000 in case of growth.

Infra notes (what likely matters)
- We discovered that the in-house batching layer holds requests for up to 120ms waiting for batch completion during low traffic windows — that explains some of the tail inflation.
- GPU utilization is low on the A100 nodes during peak — we suspect serialization and model-server inefficiencies.

Files attached
- call-recording-20260115-1530.zoom.txt (link to internal recording & short transcript)
- perf CSV you referenced (thanks for pulling it in)

We’re available for the deep-dive on Jan 20 (flexible morning PST) or Jan 21 (afternoon PST). Rishi, looped in — any initial thoughts?

— Oliver
Head of Product Engineering | FinAgile
Oliver.Chen@finagile.com

On Fri, Jan 16, 2026 at 09:12 AM Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@finagile.com> wrote:
> Camila — this is very helpful, thanks for the thorough read. Quick clarifications and a couple of notes from our infra team after running the perf snapshot overnight.

Thanks for the context and for sharing the perf traces. A few immediate hypotheses and what I’d like to cover in the deep-dive: 

Immediate hypotheses
- Batching delay (120ms) is a major contributor to p95 inflation. We can evaluate continuous batching vs fixed-window batching to reduce wait times.
- Model-server CPU serialization (pre/post processing) likely causing low GPU utilization — adding asynchronous preproc / offloading tokenization could help.
- First-byte latency is often dominated by I/O and model init on cold workers; prefix caching + warm pool + tiny instance ergonomics can push p95 down substantially.

Technical deep-dive agenda (60m)
1) Quick intro & confirm success criteria (5m)
2) Walkthrough of your current request path and traces (10m)
3) Profiling results we ran on the perf CSV (I’ll share a short profiler extract) — focus on batching wait, CPU vs GPU time (15m)
4) Options: runtime config changes (continuous batching, KV cache), model variants & quantization tradeoffs, and recommended infra topology for streaming (20m)
5) PoC scope & next steps (10m)

PoC proposal (short)
- Duration: 3 weeks
- Goals: validate p95 first-byte < 200ms at 400 sustained streams; measure stall rates; quantify cost delta for a quantized variant.
- Minimal infra: 2-GPU test pool (mixed A100 + T4 for cost sim), dedicated warm pool, and a small traffic generator that mimics your agent assist behavior.

Prep items (Oliver/Priya)
- A short trace with request headers and timestamps for 10 sessions (we’ll extract from the recording if you prefer)
- Access to the perf CSV in Drive (we have it)
- Any constraints on adding instrumentation or a test worker for the PoC

I’ll create a meeting invite for Jan 20 morning PST and attach a short pre-read with profiler snippets. Camila / Marissa — I’ll lean on you to coordinate calendar and PoC doc review.

Rishi Malhotra
